proposed_comments.title: Honor cached revocation when verifying the peer signer
proposed_comments.body:
### Honor cached revocation when verifying the peer signer

**Severity:** `high`

The new peer verifier currently disables revocation in the custom signer chain, so a binary signed with the same PowerToys leaf would still pass after that certificate or key is revoked. Please mirror the existing native verifier here: use cached/offline revocation, reject known revocation, and tolerate only the expected unknown/offline revocation states so the check stays network-free without trusting a revoked signer.

confidence.rationale: The upstream file still sets X509RevocationMode.NoCheck, while the converged fork branch switches to cached offline revocation and the refreshed Copilot loop plus targeted tests stay green.

proposed_comments.title: Throttle the repeated IPC rejection and retry log paths
proposed_comments.body:
### Throttle the repeated IPC rejection and retry log paths

**Severity:** `medium`

Rejected or squatted pipe connections can currently reconnect in a tight loop and emit a log entry on every attempt. Please keep the retry/backoff behavior, but rate-limit both the rejected-client log and the exception retry log by time so an unexpected same-user caller cannot drive sustained CPU churn and unbounded log growth.

confidence.rationale: The current review branch adds a 250 ms backoff plus strict time-based throttling for both rejection and exception paths, and the final fresh Copilot review no longer raises the resource-growth issue.

proposed_comments.title: Cache only accepted peer verification results by process instance
proposed_comments.body:
### Cache only accepted peer verification results by process instance

**Severity:** `medium`

The current implementation rebuilds signer trust on every reconnect, but an unbounded cache of rejected callers would let short-lived unexpected processes accumulate state for the lifetime of MWB. Cache the verified peer verdict by PID plus process creation time for the expected Settings/MWB pair, and retain only accepted entries so reconnects stay cheap without turning rejected callers into a memory-growth vector.

confidence.rationale: The converged fork branch proves that accepted-only PID+creation-time caching addresses both repeated signature work and cache growth, and Copilot accepted the change on the final zero-comment pass.

proposed_comments.title: Keep generated certificate fixtures inside the issuer validity window
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep generated certificate fixtures inside the issuer validity window

**Severity:** `medium`

The new certificate-building helpers derive child certificates from `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(7)`. Near a second boundary, that can make the child `notAfter` slightly later than the issuer's `NotAfter`, which turns the new revocation-chain test into a flaky failure. Bind each child certificate's validity window to the issuing certificate instead of recomputing it from the current clock.

confidence.rationale: This failure reproduced directly during targeted validation on the current head, and the converged fork branch fixed it by deriving each child notAfter from the issuer certificate before the rerun passed 23 of 23 settings IPC tests.
